long_biography.plain_text:
William Goldfarb wanted Colby students to have an intellectual meeting place beyond their classes. His founding gift helped establish the Goldfarb Center for Public Affairs in 2003. Professor Sandy Maisel translated the concept into programmes, creating a student governing board and encouraging students to organise and promote events. Discussions sometimes continued over dinner.

The centre also brought academic research into public use. Its early activities included the Colby Economic Outlook, a newsletter forecasting the American and Maine economies. Economics students maintained the forecasting models under Professor Michael Donihue, combining classroom work with estimates intended for policymakers in Washington and Augusta.
